Lemma
[One-dimensional Cauchy uniqueness for waves] \group Energy Methods

Let $u,v \in C^2(\R ^2)$ solve the one-dimensional wave equation on all of $\R ^2$. If $u=v$ and $u_t=v_t$ on $\R \times \{ t=0\} $, then $u=v$ everywhere.
Proof

Subtract the two solutions and write $w=u-v$. The resulting wave has zero displacement and velocity at time zero. Differentiating the identity $w(x,0)=0$ in $x$ gives $w_x(x,0)=0$, so both characteristic Riemann invariants $w_t\pm w_x$ vanish on the initial line. The wave equation makes these invariants constant along their characteristic lines, hence both vanish everywhere. Thus $w_t=0$; constancy along vertical time lines and $w(x,0)=0$ give $w\equiv 0$.

□
